title: Lemon granita
summary: Sicilian-style lemon ice, scraped into fine crystals as it freezes: no machine, sharp and very refreshing.
steps: Warm 1 cup of the water with the allulose and zest, stirring until dissolved. Take off the heat and leave 10 minutes.
Strain, then stir in the remaining water and the lemon juice. Pour into a metal baking dish about 20 x 30 cm (8 x 12 in).
Freeze for 45 minutes, then rake the icy edges into the middle with a fork.
Repeat every 30 minutes for about 3 hours, until the whole dish is fine, fluffy crystals.
Serve straight away in chilled glasses, or cover and keep frozen and rake again before serving.
tips: Allulose gives softer crystals than erythritol, which freezes into hard shards.

origin.history: Sicilians long harvested snow from Mount Etna and other peaks, stored it in pits, and served it shaved with fruit syrups; a link to the sherbets of the island's Arab period is often suggested but is traditional rather than documented. The granita made by freezing and stirring a flavoured syrup, now eaten across Sicily, was established by the nineteenth century.
